Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

current adjective

present, of now

also currently, the current situation, contemporary, present-day, in current use

classical

Gell. 1.10.4: loquere verbīs praesentibus, words now in use (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BC 1.52: inopiā praesentis, sed etiam futūrī temporis (Lewis & Short)

praesēns, praesentis

adjective, third declension, one ending

present, current (as against past or future)

Of the speaker’s own time Latin rarely uses praesēns alone, and says hic instead (Lewis & Short): hōc tempore, at the current time.

Other words

  • 1hic: short i (Lewis & Short hīc, haec, hōc, marking the heavy syllable as a long vowel). De Vaan 284, s.v. hic: the nominative is *hi-ke, so the vowel is short and the syllable heavy (hicc, p. 102, s.v. -ce); the adverb hīc, here, is the old locative *hoi-ke.

    hic1, haec, hoc — this, the present (of time)

    pronoun · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 154: quondam … hōc tempore

    The current year is hic annus; currently, hōc tempore or nunc (see now).

  • ūsitātus, ūsitāta, ūsitātum — current, in general use (of words and customs)

    adjective · also used · classical · Traupman 299: current (in general use), ūsitātus; Cic. Fin. 3.4: vocābula (Lewis & Short)

    See normal.

  • hodiernus, hodierna, hodiernum — of today, present-day

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 4.7: ex hodiernō ejus ēdictō (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. modern, contemporary, current

    Of this very day; the wider sense “present-day” is rare and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short), and Morgan–Owens’s examples are Tertullian’s.

Examples

  • vīve ergō mōribus praeteritīs, loquere verbīs praesentibus

    live, then, by the ways of the past, but speak the words of the presentGell. 1.10.4

  • adnotābant seniōrēs, quibus ōtiōsum est vetera et praesentia contendere

    the older men, who have time to compare past and present, remarkedTac. Ann. 13.3

See also now, today, normal.
